title: The Nav channel bench series: Plasmid preparation☆
author: Feldman, Lossin

steps.title: Transform Stbl2 cells with plasmid
steps.instruction: Ice‑chill 2 µl (20 ng) plasmid DNA in the bottom of a Falcon tube; thaw a 25 µl aliquot of Stbl2 competent cells on ice for 5 min, add the cells to the chilled DNA and mix gently by pipette tip agitation.

steps.title: Recover and plate transformed cells
steps.instruction: Incubate the DNA‑cell mixture on ice for 25 min, heat‑shock in a 42 °C water bath for 40 s, immediately return to ice for 2 min, add 400 µl room‑temperature SOC, shake in a pre‑warmed 30 °C incubator for 90 min, then plate 50 µl on one pre‑warmed LB plate and 250 µl on a second pre‑warmed LB plate, both containing antibiotic at half‑standard concentration.

steps.title: Incubate plates until colonies appear
steps.instruction: Allow plates to sit right‑side up at room temperature for 10 min, then invert and incubate upside‑down in a dedicated 30 °C incubator for several days until two distinct colony populations (large fast‑growers and tiny slow‑growers) are visible.

steps.title: Pick slow colonies and start mini cultures
steps.instruction: After several days, inspect the LB plates, select suitable slow‑growing small colonies, and using autoclaved toothpicks inoculate several 3 ml LB mini cultures (half‑standard antibiotic concentration) with the colonies.

steps.title: Grow mini cultures and perform miniprep
steps.instruction: Shake the mini cultures at 30 °C for 2–3 days until turbid; process 1.5 ml of each mini culture with the available miniprep kit using water for the final elution step, and store the remaining mini‑culture at 4 °C.

steps.title: Digest miniprep DNA and run gel
steps.instruction: Set up 20 µl restriction digests using only restriction buffer, the appropriate enzyme, and the miniprep eluate; separate the digests by standard agarose gel electrophoresis and identify the expected restriction fingerprint.

steps.title: Scale up to maxi cultures
steps.instruction: From the correct fingerprint, inoculate two to three 200 ml LB maxi cultures (half‑standard antibiotic concentration) with 200 µl of the corresponding mini‑culture (1:1000 dilution).

steps.title: Grow maxi cultures and perform customized maxi prep
steps.instruction: Shake the 200 ml cultures at 30 °C overnight; process each culture according to the maxi‑prep kit instructions, but customize the final TE‑buffer elution by passing the eluate from the first silica column through a second (and a third, if three maxi cultures were processed), adjusting the volume with additional TE buffer as needed.

steps.title: Quantify DNA and assess concentration for sequencing
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration by spectrophotometry and confirm identity by restriction fingerprinting; if yield is low, keep the initial elution volume small to obtain a high concentration (sequencing facilities often request >1 µg/µl for dsDNA >10 kb, but successful sequencing has been achieved down to 100 ng/µl). Dilute to the facility’s requested concentration if necessary.

steps.title: Sequence plasmid and verify data
steps.instruction: Perform full‑length sequencing of the Nav channel plasmid using primer walking with 600–800 bp intervals; process chromatograms with Nucleics’ online PeakTrace application, align reads to the appropriate NM RefSeq or LRG reference, visually confirm base calls, re‑sequence any ambiguous regions in both directions, and use the provided primer list. Once certified, the plasmid can be used for transfection or mutagenesis.
